en.headline: Customs seize 134 suspected slimming vials in Tuen Mun case
en.dek: RTHK reported that officers found 54 vials in a Japan air-mail parcel on 2 October, then a further 80 at a Tuen Mun flat, and bailed a 30-year-old woman.
body: Hong Kong Customs has seized 134 injection vials suspected to contain Part 1 poisons and marketed as weight-loss products, with an estimated value of about HK$100,000, RTHK reported on Monday.

Officers inspecting the Air Mail Centre on 2 October found 54 suspected controlled slimming vials in a parcel that had arrived from Japan. The same day they carried out a controlled delivery to the recipient’s address in Tuen Mun, arrested a 30-year-old woman, and seized a further 80 vials at the flat, the report said.
The arrested woman has been released on bail. Customs said the investigation is continuing.

The report did not set out the charging decision. Separate customs guidance on unlicensed imports of pharmaceutical products says an offence under the Import and Export Ordinance can bring a fine of up to HK$500,000 and two years’ imprisonment.

zh.headline: 海關檢134支懷疑減肥針劑 屯門拘女子
zh.dek: 港台報道，關員本月2日在空郵中心檢獲54支來自日本的懷疑針劑，同日在屯門住所再檢80支，30歲女收件人獲准保釋。
body: 香港電台報道，海關檢獲134支懷疑含有第一部毒藥的減肥針劑，估計市值約10萬元。
報道指，關員本月2日在空郵中心查驗一件由日本抵港的郵包，檢獲54支懷疑受管制減肥針劑。同日採取監控遞送行動，在屯門收貨住宅拘捕30歲女收件人，並在單位再檢獲80支同類針劑。
被捕女子現獲准保釋，案件仍在調查。
報道未有交代檢控決定。海關過往就無牌進口藥劑產品指出，觸犯《進出口條例》最高可被判罰款50萬元及監禁兩年。
